column1: When it opened in 1984, the Costco on West Dimond Boulevard in Anchorage did not seem like the future of food.
column2: A glorified shed the color of stale coffee, the warehouse offered the sort of products and deals Alaskans go crazy for: mammoth quantities of staples like peanut butter and tomato sauce, along with local favorites such as caribou sausage.
column3: When it opened in 1984, the Costco on West Dimond Boulevard in Anchorage did not seem like the future of food. column4: There's something edgy about the inventory, too: neoprene survival suits, meat grinders, gun safes.
